reconcile.connective: Gill reads Luke's perplexity and Mark's firm identification as successive stages of the same episode: Herod's initial doubt gave way to settled conviction once his guilty conscience took hold.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells, in the Skeptic's Annotated Bible, lists Matthew 14:1-2 and Mark 6:16's flat "It is John" against Luke 9:9's "but who is this?" as two different, incompatible answers Herod gives to who Jesus is.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Did Herod think Jesus was John the Baptist?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/herod.html)
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (1999), contra/herod.html

excerpts.excerpt_text: These different sentiments of the people concerning Jesus, greatly perplexed the mind of Herod, as appears from Luk 9:7, for it was first given out by others, and not by Herod, that John the Baptist was risen from the dead; which he hearing of, gave him great uneasiness: … At first he could not receive it, that since he was beheaded by him, he should be restored to life; but hearing of the miracles that were done by him, his conscience accused him, his fancy worked, and at length he firmly believed it, that he must be risen: …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Gill explicitly names Luke 9:7 and stitches it to Mark 6:16 as one continuous psychological process (perplexed doubt hardening into firm belief), directly addressing why the two Gospels present Herod's mental state so differently.

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63), on Mark 6:16
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill's own note on Mark 6:16 explicitly cross-references Luke 9:7 and reconciles the two by reading Herod's Lukan perplexity as the earlier stage of the same episode that hardens into Matthew/Mark's firm identification. (Haley's An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible was checked directly via full-text search on the archive.org djvu.txt for 'Herod' and 'John the Baptist' and does not treat this passage at all, so Gill is used per the contract's fallback clause.)
